title: deferred-eviction-thresholds-and-prefetch-hint-propagation-for-paged-kv
creator: Ayesha Kumar
description: Design and prototype a deferred-eviction policy for the paged/blocked KV cache that integrates per-request prefetch hints from the continuous batching scheduler. Goal: reduce redundant GPU<->host transfers during high-concurrency continuous batching while bounding tail latency and memory pressure.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype implements a deferred-eviction threshold per slab block aligned to batch-affinity windows
Prefetch hint propagation path from batching scheduler to KV allocator exists and is exercised in unit/e2e tests
Synthetic trace tests show >=25% reduction in PCIe transfer bytes for long-context (8k+) streaming workloads compared to baseline eviction
End-to-end p50 token latency regression <5ms and p99 regression <15ms under 95th percentile load
Safety: fallback to immediate eviction when GPU memory pressure crosses emergency threshold
notes: Motivation: continuous batching aggregates partially overlapping prefixes from many requests. Current eager eviction can oscillate residency when adjacent batches touch similar contexts, producing back-and-forth host<->GPU transfers.

Key idea: when a block is a candidate for eviction, defer reclaim for a small time window (eviction grace) if incoming prefetch hints indicate near-future reuse. This reduces churn for hot-but-not-always hot regions typical in streaming/completion-heavy traffic.
Eviction grace should decay with token distance and be bounded by available resident memory headroom to avoid OOMs.

Prefetch hints are lightweight per-request metadata propagated from continuous-batching scheduler: (block_id, estimated-next-token-offset, confidence). Hints are aggregated in short windows and translated into temporal priorities for blocks.

We must avoid starving eviction when sustained memory pressure increases. Two-tier thresholds: soft_defer_threshold triggers grace; hard_reclaim_threshold forces immediate eviction and bypasses hints.

Block alignment: use existing block size (64KB-aligned) but add a sub-block hotness counter to avoid over-defer for partially hot blocks. Sub-block counters are maintained in compact bitmaps to limit metadata overhead.

Interaction with kernel scheduling: prefetch urgency influences PCIe transfer prioritization. Hints mark transfers as high/low priority so the host-side IO scheduler can reorder DMA in-flight operations within a short window.
Security: hints are internal only and do not contain user data. They are opaque identifiers mapping to block IDs assigned by the allocator. No customer-visible surface change.
Fallbacks: if PCIe bandwidth saturates, we throttle prefetches and reduce grace windows; also integrate with existing backpressure token-affinity paths to limit concurrent prefetches per-model.
This design intentionally balances additional metadata cost vs reduced transfer volume. We estimate 1-2% resident metadata overhead per GPU for the hint aggregator tables.

Open question: how to tune grace window size across different model families and sequence length distributions. We will run A/B tests with adaptive controllers that adjust windows based on observed transfer churn rate.
decisions: Use time-based eviction grace (milliseconds) instead of count-based to align with continuous-batching wall-clock behavior
Add compact sub-block hotness bitmaps (64 bits per block) rather than per-token counters to minimize memory overhead
Implement hint aggregation in the scheduler process (host-side) to avoid cross-GPU synchronization latency; aggregate per-host and per-model
Expose two tunables: soft_defer_threshold_ms and hard_reclaim_threshold_bytes (per-GPU). Defaults: 25ms and 512MB respectively for initial rollout
Integrate hint priority into existing PCIe DMA queue; do not add a new transport channel
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Spike completed. Measured churn on production sampling (chatstream traces) shows 30-45% redundant transfers for 6-10k contexts under the current eager-evict policy.
2026-02-18: Prototype allocator branch created (github.com/redwood-inference/serving/compare/evict-defer-147258). Initial unit tests for block bitmap correctness added.
2026-02-24: Scheduler hook PR posted (github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/512) to emit prefetch hints. Hook currently toggled behind feature flag 'hint-propagation'.

2026-03-02: End-to-end bench with synthetic trace: 28% PCIe bytes saved, p50 latency +3ms, p99 +10ms under 80% load. Memory headroom stress test identified corner case where multiple mid-hot blocks caused headroom underestimation leading to hard reclaim spikes.
2026-03-08: Implemented emergency reclaim bypass and per-host aggregated watermark to stabilize corner case. Re-ran bench: bytes saved 26%, p50 +2ms, p99 +8ms. Tests added for emergency path.
2026-03-11: Preparing RFC for design review and performance gating. Draft design doc uploaded to Drive (link below). Planning to shepherd to In Review by 2026-03-18.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Add hint propagation interface to scheduler and aggregator (host). Feature-flagged. Unit tests for serialization and loss-tolerance.
Phase 2: Implement deferred eviction policy and sub-block bitmap in allocator. Add soft/hard thresholds and emergency reclaim path. Bench harnesses for synthetic and sampled traces.
Phase 3: Add DMA priority tagging and host IO scheduler hint translation. Run GPU-level perf and thermal tests.
Phase 4: Canary rollout on a subset of Dedicated clusters. Collect p50/p99 token latency, PCIe bytes, memory headroom metrics. Iterate tuning controller.
Phase 5: Full rollout and add console cost/latency dashboards and runbook for incident response
Estimated work split: 40% allocator, 30% scheduler, 15% IO integration, 15% testing/telemetry
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Deferred evictions could delay reclamation and trigger OOM under bursty allocation patterns. Mitigation: strict hard_reclaim_threshold bytes and immediate bypass when GPU free memory below emergency watermark.
Risk: Incorrect hint aggregation could bias priorities and reduce hit rate. Mitigation: keep hints advisory, apply only when confidence >= 0.6 and decay unobserved hints quickly.
Risk: Added metadata increases host-GPU sync cost. Mitigation: compact representations (bitmaps) and batched updates in scheduler windows.
Risk: PCIe priority tagging may interact poorly with cloud host drivers. Mitigation: keep tagging optional and fall back to FIFO DMA ordering if host driver rejects hints.
